name: Tearing
desc: A tear running through a fibrous sheet, held in macro with the camera riding the tip so it never finishes — the mat whitens under strain ahead of the crack, separates along one ragged path whose two deckle edges interlock exactly because they were once the same edge, and behind it single fibres bridge the widening gap, going slack, drawing taut, then snapping and recoiling into dangling pull-out; cream rag paper, carbon-fibre laminate under an electron beam, translucent parchment, backlit mat or a flat conservator's loss diagram.

energy.doc: raking-lamp gain, fibre brightness and how hard the process zone whitens ahead of the tip

scale.doc: macro magnification — max nearly triples the mat and resolves individual fibres bridging the gap

speed.doc: how fast the sheet feeds past the tip — the tear rate (0.2 still advances)

density.doc: how many fibres bridge the gap — a sparse weak mat or a dense stubborn one

gap.doc: how far the two flaps pull apart behind the tip — sets how long fibres survive before they snap

hue.doc: hue of the sheet stock — warm rag cream through cold synthetic

y.doc: where the tear line sits vertically in frame

style.doc: aesthetic: warm cream rag paper in raking light / carbon-fibre laminate as a cold greyscale electron micrograph / translucent parchment with collagen glow / backlit so the mat glows and every fibre is a shadow / flat hatched conservator's loss diagram with no light at all

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the tear path, the deckle and every fibre's slack and strength
